data.narrative:
Carbon Robotics, a Series C robotics and manufacturing company founded by Paul Mikesell, has raised $177M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of 9 private peers and 1 public comparable in the robotics and manufacturing sector, including companies at Series B through Series D stages.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis uses the $177M total raised as a baseline and applies a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical for Series C advancement, yielding $301M. Peer-median analysis examines 7 same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables—including Exotec ($2.0B, Series D), Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B, Series B), Dexterity ($1.6B, Series B), and Hadrian ($1.6B, Series D)—producing a median valuation of $1.6B with a range of $1.0B to $2.0B.

The two methods diverge materially. Stage-progression anchors to capital invested and implies $301M; peer-median reflects trading multiples at adjacent stages and implies $1.6B. Triangulation across both methods supports a range of $256M (low) to $1.9B (high), with a median of $975M. The wide dispersion reflects genuine uncertainty: stage-progression methodology underweights market comparables, while peer-median may overweight late-stage inflation. Further diligence on Carbon Robotics' revenue, growth trajectory, and specific positioning within the peer set would narrow this range materially.
